summary: Isabelle Ratié is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Paris 1, under Marie-Claude Porcher, Lyne Bansat-Boudon, and Alexis Sanderson. She held positions at Leipzig, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and Collège de France.

Isaiah Berlin worked in philosophy and history. Educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford, he spent his academic career at the University of Oxford from approximately 1932 to 1997.

Isaline Blew Horner was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Cambridge under Kenneth J. Saunders and Caroline Rhys Davids. She held library and governing roles at Newnham College and served as Pali Text Society Honorary Secretary.
Isamu Kanaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as a professor at Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College, attested in 1976.
Isao Nishitani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history affiliated with Sennyu-ji in 2016 and an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, attested in 2026.

Iselin Frydenlund is a researcher in Buddhist studies and religious studies who held posts as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and a research fellow at the University of Oslo, both attested in 2016.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Sanskrit College. He worked at Fort William College, served as Assistant Secretary at Sanskrit College, and became Direktor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1851.

Isidor Isaac Scheftelowitz was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. After completing a Ph.D. under Adalbert Bezzenberger at Königsberg, he taught at the University of Cologne and held a post at Balliol College, Oxford.

Ismael Quiles Sánchez was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Colegio Máximo de San Ignacio and other institutions, he served as Vice-Rector and Prorector at Universidad del Salvador and visited Georgetown University.

Iso Kern is a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Louvain and Heidelberg. He held academic posts at KU Leuven, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bern, alongside teaching appointments in Zurich and Fribourg.
Issaien Ikeyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies who held professorships at Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji Junior College, attested in 1976.
Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and subsequently served there as a professor.
Issei Yamakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Sophia University and a master's course at Aichi Gakuin University.
István Tamaskó was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna and Göttingen, where he was taught by Heinrich Ewald. In 1838, he became a professor at the Evangelical Lutheran Lyceum.

Italo Pizzi was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological scholar who earned a doctorate at Pisa. He taught at Florence, Naples, and the University of Turin, where he became a professor of Persian language and literature.

Ithamar Theodor is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Wolfson College, Oxford, and was a visiting fellow at Clare Hall and the Divinity Faculty at the University of Cambridge.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a linguist and Japanologist educated at Teachers College, Columbia University, currently attested in 2026 as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington.

Ivan Ivanovich Zarubin was an Iranian and linguistics scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg and Kharkiv. He worked at Kunstkamera, held a professorship at Saint Petersburg State University, and served at the Institute of Linguistics.
Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and later served on its Faculty of Oriental Studies from circa 1871 to 1890.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Albrecht Weber, later serving as Privatdozent and Professor at Saint Petersburg State University from 1869.
